<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **45** documentable anchor(s).

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **32** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `25e4e81da1c6337fed13b984f00a322b5ddd2813` — the merge of head `bf7e3295e9ed0c6ca46217e172e25ed5f4aeaee7` into base `87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 25e4e81da1c6337fed13b984f00a322b5ddd2813 && git checkout 25e4e81da1c6337fed13b984f00a322b5ddd2813
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337 bf7e3295e9ed0c6ca46217e172e25ed5f4aeaee7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337 && git merge --no-ff bf7e3295e9ed0c6ca46217e172e25ed5f4aeaee7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Both items from the preliminary epic review (6729460160) are fixed at head `054df525`.**

**Item 1: picklist referrer with more than one packaged contributor.**
- `picklistReferrerOf` now returns every packaged `own`/`extend` contributor whose own declaration names that picklist on the field, each package once. It no longer keeps only the last one.
- The new `SchemaRegistry.resolveFieldPicklistOptions` asks R once per referrer. The field is served only when every referrer resolves to the same holder (`sameHolder`). Any other outcome serves no options, so the validator refuses the field's values: one referrer refused or reaching nothing, or two reaching different holders.
- The boot audit already judges each packaged contributor separately (`auditPicklistReferences`). So each referrer whose own resolution refuses is named, with R's sentence and its candidates.
- Under phase 1, a disagreement can only be one referrer resolved and another refused. A package caller never reaches the environment's item, and a picklist name has at most one package holder.
- Pin in `engine-picklist.test.ts`, "two packages writing one field's reference: served no options unless BOTH reach the list (no fold-order pick)". The owner has no dependency on the list's package and the extender, folded last, does. The field is served no options, and the audit names `com.test.pkg`. A CONTROL test has both depending on it and the list is served.
- Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, last-wins put back): the pin goes red, 1 failed / 31 passed. Restored with blob == HEAD.

**Item 2: the install judge's artifact-wide `declared.has` short-circuit.**
- The artifact-wide set is gone. Each reference short-circuits only on its own manifest's lists (`collectManifestPicklistNames(manifest)`). Everything else is answered by `picklistReferenceVerdict(…, ordered)`.
- `withPendingManifests` now also lists each pending manifest's `picklists` as held by that manifest's package. Before, it overlaid only `getPackage`. So R judges a sibling's list through the referrer's declared closure, the way the served field will once the artifact registers. Extension targets are still judged caller-less.
- Pins in `plugin-picklist-boot-audit.test.ts`, describe "the picklist install door — a sibling in the same artifact (ADR-0150 D3)":
  - A two-package artifact whose app has no dependency on the sibling holding the list is refused. The refusal names `package "com.test.suite.lists"` and nothing registers. This is the N1 arm, marked as pending the ruling.
  - CONTROL: the same artifact with the dependency registers and is served the list.
- Ablation (the artifact-wide set put back): the refusal pin goes red, 1 failed / 10 passed. Restored with blob == HEAD.

**Runs on `054df525`:**
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck && … test` under the lock: 571 files passed and 11659 tests passed. The same two tests are red as before, both still held: the N1 residual test and the core-boundary ratchet (R2 #31733).
- eslint on `packages/objectql/src` (`--no-inline-config`): exit 0.

Still owed for the final head: merge `main` once R2 #31733 lands, then the gates and the dogfood battery again on that head.

**Test Core (1/8) on `054df525`** ([job 128918340435](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42541586593/job/128918340435)): three tests are red in `@objectstack/cli`. I reproduced all three locally (`packages/cli`, `vitest run` on the two files: 3 failed / 12 passed).

- `seed-record-values.test.ts` › "judges a picklist-bound field against the options the stack's picklist resolves". **This one is this PR's, and it is not declared yet.** The cli judge registers the stack's picklists package-less, and its objects through `ObjectQL#registerObject` with no package, which defaults to `'__runtime__'`. R treats `'__runtime__'` as a package, so D3 (a) refuses the environment list. This is a narrowing wider than the declared one. I've put it to the epic seat with options, and I'm recommending treating the compatibility default `'__runtime__'` as a package-less referrer. Nothing is pushed until that is ruled.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bf7e3295e9ed0c6ca46217e172e25ed5f4aeaee7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.boot-parity.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-picklist.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-objects.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/picklist-resolution.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin-picklist-boot-audit.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts + packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/package-closure.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/seed-record-values.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/metadata/src/endpoint-matcher.ts, packages/metadata/src/stored-envelope.ts, docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md (read on `origin/main` fdfcc7ab, never reviewed)

Inputs: card #31678 (body and all 10 comments, rulings 6728478528, 6728613177 and 6729820123 included), PR #31731 body and file list, the net diff of `bf7e3295` against its merge-base with `main` (`2b752aa4`, 10 files, +837/-75), and the 54 check-runs on the head: 37 success, 17 skipped (UI, docs, opt-in and draft-only legs), 0 failure, 0 pending. `main` has moved 6 lines in `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` since the merge-base (ADR-0150 D8 ledger backfill at `kernel:ready`, #31727); it touches neither hunk of this PR and GitHub reports the head mergeable and clean.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged against ADR-0150 D3/D4 on `main` and R/R2 as merged (`resolvePackageScopedHolders` in `@objectstack/core`, `packageResolutionClosure` in `@objectstack/metadata-core`):

1. **A served object's packaged field resolves its `picklist` from the package that declares the field** (`picklistReferrerOf` → `resolveFieldPicklistOptions` → `resolvePicklistOptions(name, caller)` → `resolvePackageScopedName`). Own list → unique holder in the declared closure plus `sys` → refusal naming every candidate. The referrer is read off the `own`/`extend` contributors whose own declaration names that list on that field, tenant-authored layers excluded; a reference no packaged layer writes resolves caller-less. **Right**: D3's rule and D3's overlay sentence ("a reference written in an environment-authored overlay is the environment's reference"), no first-registered fallback and no fold-order pick anywhere on the path.
2. **Two packaged layers writing one field's reference: served only when every referrer reaches the same holder, else no options.** **Right** by red line 2 (ambiguity reported, never guessed). See ④ F2 for the one arm the audit does not name.
3. **`resolvePicklistOptions(name)` with no caller keeps its answer** (environment item first, else the unique holder): the save door (`protocol-save-door-refusals.ts` line 688) and `seed-record-values.ts` line 129 call it caller-less and are unchanged. **Right**: D3's caller-less rule; the CONTROL pin shows the same list as on `main`.
4. **`findUnresolvedPicklistReferences()` narrows its set**: an `outside-closure` refusal leaves it and goes to the new `findOutsideClosurePicklistReferences()`; the boot throws for not-found and ambiguous, warns for outside-closure. **Right** by ruling N2 (6728478528) and 6729820123 ("severity follows the N2 ruling").
5. **`findOrphanPicklistExtensions()` judges the target caller-less through R**; a refusal there is only an environment-wide ambiguity, named. **Right** by ruling X (6728613177).
6. **The post-seal install judge** reaches each pending reference from its own manifest's package through a registry view that overlays the pending manifests (`withPendingManifests`): own list short-circuits (D3 step 1), everything else is R's answer over the pending holders plus the installed ones, the residual owner's declared dependencies handed to the walk (`residualOwnerDependenciesOf`, which `closurePackageReader` consults only for an id `getPackage` cannot produce — the view's `getPackage` answers pending ids first, so the precedence holds). It refuses loudly with R's sentence; extension targets are judged caller-less. **Right**: D3 at a door ("a door refuses an unresolvable reference"), and the ruled N1 shape (a same-artifact sibling needs a declared dependency). No artifact-wide "declared somewhere" pass remains.
7. **`describeUnresolvedPicklistReferences` appends R's refusal sentence** per line; headline and rule id unchanged. **Right**; the CLI's parity test still matches on the headline.
8. **`assertPicklistValuesDistinct` is judged against the held extensions directly** instead of through resolution (the list is not registered yet, so nothing resolves). **Right**: same set as before for the pre-registration case.
9. **Public surface of `SchemaRegistry`** gains `picklistReferenceVerdict(name, caller?, pendingManifests?)` and `findOutsideClosurePicklistReferences()`; `resolvePicklistOptions` gains an optional `callerPackageId`; `findUnresolvedPicklistReferences`/`findOrphanPicklistExtensions` return a supertype with an optional `refusal`. `picklist-resolution.ts` gains `PicklistFieldResolver`, `UnresolvedPicklistReference`, `UnresolvedPicklistExtension`; the module is not re-exported from the package entry. All additive and backwards-compatible; the only caller outside objectql (`seed-record-values.ts`) type-checks unchanged (Type Check legs green). **Right**, and the names are the seat's call (③).
10. **`sameHolder`** compares package holders by id and `environment`/`platform` by kind. **Right**: R2's holder union carries no id on the non-package kinds.
11. **`MetadataManager.listForIndex('api')` keys the matcher's item list by (package, name)** through the private `byPackage` option; the anonymous-flow-door audit reads the same list. A package-less row under a name exactly one package holds shares the holder's slot (first entry wins, registry before loaders); a package-less row under a name no package holds is the environment's slot. **Right** by D4's picklist/api row and its customization paragraph; the matcher still keys routes by METHOD + path and resolves a duplicate path deterministically and loudly, so nothing downstream guesses. Phase-1 answers are byte-identical. See ④ F3 for the unstated two-holder arm.
12. **`loaderEntries` refactor**: `admitLoaderItems` keeps first-wins-per-name; the `loadMany` path now leaves out an item whose `name` is the empty string (the keyed path always did). Accept-set change, nil effect: no consumer's schema admits an empty name. **Right** (④ F4, accepted).
13. **Forced test edits** (two fixtures gain `dependencies`, one load-order test registers under the list's own package, the residual fixture and the CLI parity fixture declare the sibling): each is exactly the one-line fix the changeset prescribes and the ruling names ("the residual fixture gets a forced dependencies edit"). **Right**; the first-party count is stated (0 shipped, 2 test fixtures).

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/31678-picklist-by-referrer-package.md`: `@objectstack/objectql: patch`, `@objectstack/metadata: patch`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset body; BREAKING banner present with the FROM → TO behaviour and the one-line fix; ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, one marker. `Check Changeset` green twice, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` green.

- The level matches what the diff publishes: no schema key, export removal or stored shape moves; AGENTS.md Post-Task 3 gives a non-protocol narrowing `patch` with its BREAKING banner and disposition. **Right.**
- `Metadata-protocol: none` matches the diff: what an author can write is unchanged (the same `picklist` key and value parse); what moves is which list the runtime serves and a door refusal, the same shape `.changeset/31550-*` on `main` declared as `no (narrowing)` + `none` + `no-migration-prescription`, and the card's own claim (6728435375) and ruling (6728476284, "本裁只定收窄范围，不改协议形状"). **Right.**
- `@objectstack/cli` is touched in a test file only: no changeset owed. **Right.**
- The `Clause-②:` line on the PR body and the changeset agree with each other and with the narrowing face this record is served on. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and `open_questions` entry from the report (6729376780) and the PR body, answered or escalated:

- **N1 (sibling in the same artifact, no declared dependency)**: ruled 6729820123, declared dependency closure only. The head is A-shaped as the ruling requires (the residual fixture's forced edit, the install-door sibling pin, the N1 arm in the boot-warning pin). **Answered.**
- **New names (seat's call)**: `findOutsideClosurePicklistReferences`, `picklistReferenceVerdict`, the private `byPackage` option, and the three exported types. **Answered: keep (A).** Each names what it answers; none is a schema key; the report's earlier spelling `findEnvironmentHeldPicklistReferences` was already renamed on this head to the N1-correct name.
- **"Part of", not "Fixes"**: functions went to R2 by ruling S-a (6728478528) and R2 #31733 is on `main`; mapping and dataset have no package-referrer reader in the surface (ruled, same comment). The card stays open for its remainder. **Answered**; consistent with the rulings.
- **The api re-key landed in `metadata-manager.ts`, not `endpoint-matcher.ts`**: ruling S-b. **Answered.**
- **Two tests held red / lean-entry-closure red on the draft**: cleared by R2's landing; every check-run on this head is green, the body reports 0 red in objectql and metadata. **Answered by the check-runs.**
- **Gates ran on 42bdbe6c before the merge**: re-run on the head per the body's Verification section, and the head's own check-runs are the gate verdicts here. **Answered.**
- **HotCRM not measured**: carried to the S4 (#31693) upgrade report by the ruling's "blind spot carried". **Escalated as ruled; nothing for this head.**
- **The CLI author-time door still resolves a sibling's list without a declared dependency** (`packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts`, module header line 42, `judgePicklistReferences`): after this head the runtime warns at boot and refuses the same artifact at install, so `os validate` no longer foretells the install door for that one case. The ruling places the ADR-0130 narrowing (a dated note in the ADR and at line 42) with child A #31685; the inputs name no carrier for the door's code. **Escalated**: a follow-up card to the lane that owns `packages/cli` (or child A's scope confirmed to include the door), see ④ F1. Not this head's: the ruling lands E6 with "0 extra code" and the CLI source is outside the claimed surface.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing itself, against the published spec on `main`.** Two refusals are declared on the PR body and the changeset: (1) D3 (a), a package field whose list only an environment-authored item holds; (2) the general outside-closure case, a same-artifact sibling included. (1) is ADR-0150's own declared narrowing (TL;DR 7 and D3 (a)), carried to picklist by the E6 row of the execution plan: the spec's refusal made real, not a capability taken away. (2) is D3 step 3 as written ("else a refusal that lists the candidates"), applied over the declared closure that R implements; the sibling sub-case is where ADR-0130 (release artifact = co-ownership boundary) and ADR-0150 D3 disagreed, and the maintainer ruled it by meaning on 2026-11-09T01:07Z (6729820123): declared dependency closure only, child A records it in both ADRs. So the consumer refuses exactly what the accepted spec plus its ruling refuses, nothing more: a field whose package holds the list or depends on its holder is served as before, a caller-less reader is served as before, an extension still adds to the one list its target names. The severity ladder (boot warns naming every candidate, the read serves no options and the validator refuses the value, the post-seal install refuses loudly) is the ruled N2 shape, one answer at two severities, and `ctx.logger.warn` is the right level under AGENTS.md's degradation rule: the system is visibly smaller (a select with nothing to choose, a refused write), nothing claims to be persisted that is not. The boot's verdict is read at `kernel:ready`, after every package registered, so it is final (startup-registry-reads rule).

**Attempts to break it, read in the live tree:**

- *A second closure walk or a first-registered fallback hidden in objectql?* None: every picklist read in `registry.ts` routes through `picklistReferenceVerdict` → `resolvePackageScopedName`; `getItem('picklist', …)` has no remaining caller outside tests; `package-scoped-resolver.ts` and `bare-name-one-holder.ts` are untouched.
- *The pending-manifest view misreading R's inputs?* `getPackage` answers pending ids first (their `dependencies` and `namespace` are all the walk reads); `getAllPackages` drops an installed row the pending set shadows, so `kernelPackages` and the pair-widening see one row per id; `packageScopedHoldersOf` unions pending holders with installed ones (the dropped third argument only matters for bundled types, and picklist has no discriminator); `getPackageScopedItem` returns a stub for a pending holder, which only the verdict's status reads. The residual-owner pin (ablation 7) covers the one path that reaches a list only through a residual owner.
- *Environment list and package list of one name at once?* Not a reachable split: a package-less row under a name a package holds is that holder's overlay (`overlaySlotBinding`), so `getEnvironmentScopedItem` answers nothing and both the field and a caller-less extension resolve to the same holder. The D3 (a) arm needs a name no package holds, which is what the pins build.
- *Stale fold after a late package record?* `invalidateAll` runs on every picklist registration, and every production door installs the package record before its objects (`engine-registration.ts` line 268 before 276/289/317; the manifest service goes through the same facet). See F5 for the test-only order.

**Findings** (must-fix: none; should-fix: none; nits: six):
